findings.title: Insecure URL Normalization Leading to Potential Proxy Smuggling
findings.description: Removing the leading slash normalization exposes double slashes to urllib3 and downstream proxies. In the context of requests to proxied HTTP services (like corporate SSO, cloud LBs, or API gateways), sending paths starting with `//` instead of `/` can trigger proxy request smuggling or path traversal attacks. Some HTTP proxies may normalize the leading `//` incorrectly or treat it as an absolute URL (e.g., `//attacker.com/path`), leading to SSRF or open proxy attacks.
findings.suggestion: Ensure that all URL paths are normalized to begin with exactly one forward slash before being passed to urllib3 or any proxy, e.g., `url = '/' + url.lstrip('/')` or rely on urllib3's own normalization if it's safe for your target stack. Test against standard HTTP proxies to verify behavior.
